headline: Must-win game: Bangladesh face Afghanistan to keep final hopes alive
summary: After a heavy defeat to Zimbabwe, the Tigers must win and improve their net run rate to reach the tri-series final in the UAE.
details: Bangladesh faces Afghanistan today at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the UAE as part of a crucial tri-series group stage match.
The Tigers are currently in third place with a net run rate of -1.980 after suffering a massive loss to Zimbabwe in their opening game.
Afghanistan leads the table with a +3.160 net run rate following a 158-run victory over Zimbabwe.
To reach the final, Bangladesh needs not only a win but also a specific net run rate improvement. If batting first, they must win by at least 41 runs.
If chasing, the required time to win depends on the target. For example, a 200-run target must be chased in 40.2 overs, while a 300-run target must be chased in 42.2 overs.
Historically, the head-to-head record between the two teams in ODIs is perfectly balanced, with both Bangladesh and Afghanistan having won 11 matches each.

If chasing, the required time to win depends on the target. For example, a 200-run target must be chased in 40.2 overs, while a 300-run target must be chased in 42.2 overs.

headline_marked: From Nov 1, [[food business registration and licensing mandatory]] in Bangladesh
headline: From Nov 1, food business registration and licensing mandatory in Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Food Safety Authority has introduced new regulations to ensure food safety and public health, covering everyone from roadside stalls to large importers.
details: The Bangladesh Food Safety Authority has made registration and licensing mandatory for various categories of food businesses and products to protect public health and ensure food safety.
Under the 'Safe Food (Registration and Licensing) Regulations, 2026', food traders and establishments must apply for the necessary permits starting November 1.
The rules apply to a wide range of businesses, including roadside mobile stalls, small restaurants, bakeries, fruit juice shops, pastry shops, and catering services.
Registration is required for 16 categories of food businesses, while those dealing with specialized or 'super food' products will need a full license.
Compulsory licensing is required for those producing or importing infant formula, special diets for the elderly, and medical-purpose foods.
Other regulated items include genetically modified foods, organic foods, irradiated foods, and foods with specific health claims.
Operating a food business without the required registration or license will be considered a punishable offense under the Safe Food Act, 2013.
The permits will be valid for three years and must be renewed after that period.
caption:
From roadside Pitha stalls to large importers, all food businesses in Bangladesh must now register or get a license by Nov 1.

Compulsory licensing is required for those producing or importing infant formula, special diets for the elderly, and medical-purpose foods.

Other regulated items include genetically modified foods, organic foods, irradiated foods, and foods with specific health claims.

Operating a food business without the required registration or license will be considered a punishable offense under the Safe Food Act, 2013.
